properties.name: Zeus
properties.description: King of the Olympian gods, ruler of Mount Olympus, and god of sky and thunder. Known for his affairs that produced demigods.

properties.name: Athena
properties.description: Goddess of wisdom, strategic warfare, and crafts. Born fully armored from Zeus's head. Patron of Athens, protector of heroes.

properties.name: Poseidon
properties.description: God of the sea, earthquakes, and horses. Brother of Zeus. His anger caused storms and earthquakes. Creator of horses.

properties.name: Hades
properties.description: God of the underworld and the dead. Not evil but stern and just. Abducted Persephone. Rich from underground metals and gems.

properties.name: Apollo
properties.description: God of sun, music, poetry, prophecy, and healing. Twin brother of Artemis. Leader of the Muses. Oracle at Delphi was his.

properties.name: Ares
properties.description: God of war and violence, unpopular among gods and mortals. Lover of Aphrodite. Represented the brutal aspect of warfare.

properties.name: Aphrodite
properties.description: Goddess of love, beauty, and desire. Born from sea foam. Her powers could overwhelm gods and mortals alike. Started the Trojan War.

properties.name: Hermes
properties.description: Messenger of the gods, guide of souls to the underworld. Patron of travelers, thieves, and merchants. Invented the lyre on his first day.

properties.name: Artemis
properties.description: Virgin goddess of the hunt, moon, and wilderness. Twin sister of Apollo. Protector of young girls and animals.

properties.name: Hephaestus
properties.description: God of the forge and fire. Lame smith who created divine weapons and automata. Husband of Aphrodite. Built the palaces of Olympus.

properties.name: Demeter
properties.description: Goddess of the harvest and agriculture. Her grief over Persephone's abduction caused winter. Central to the Eleusinian Mysteries.

properties.name: Dionysus
properties.description: God of wine, ecstasy, and theater. Born twice — once from his mother and once from Zeus's thigh. His cult involved ecstatic ritual.

properties.name: Prometheus
properties.description: Titan who stole fire from the gods and gave it to humanity, enabling civilization. Punished by Zeus — chained to a rock where an eagle ate his liver daily.

properties.name: Heracles
properties.description: Greatest hero of Greek mythology. Son of Zeus and Alcmene. Completed twelve impossible labors. Achieved immortality through suffering.

properties.name: Achilles
properties.description: Greatest warrior of the Trojan War. Son of Peleus and Thetis. Nearly invulnerable except his heel. Chose glory and short life over obscurity and long life.

properties.name: Odysseus
properties.description: King of Ithaca, cleverest of the Greeks. Conceived the Trojan Horse. Spent ten years returning home. Master of deception and survival.

properties.name: Hera
properties.description: Queen of the Olympian gods, wife of Zeus. Goddess of marriage and childbirth. Known for her jealous rage against Zeus's lovers and their children.

properties.name: Persephone
properties.description: Queen of the Underworld and goddess of spring. Daughter of Demeter. Her annual return causes spring; her descent brings winter.

properties.name: Pan
properties.description: God of the wild, shepherds, and rustic music. Half-goat, half-man. His shout caused 'panic' in enemies. Played reed pipes in Arcadian mountains.

properties.name: Hecate
properties.description: Triple-formed goddess of magic, crossroads, and the night. Guardian of thresholds. Aided Demeter in searching for Persephone.

properties.name: Eros
properties.description: God of desire and erotic love. In early tradition, a primordial force that emerged from Chaos. Later depicted as Aphrodite's mischievous son with bow and arrows.

properties.name: Nike
properties.description: Winged goddess of victory. Companion of Athena and Zeus. Inspired the famous statue Winged Victory of Samothrace and the modern brand.

properties.name: Kronos
properties.description: Titan king who devoured his children to prevent prophecy. Zeus escaped and overthrew him. In Roman tradition (as Saturn), ruled a lost Golden Age.
